M16.intro: Performance runs your performance year: the set-up (rating scales, competencies, KRAs, KPI formulas, templates), goal sheets, review cycles with self, manager and approver reviews, calibration and published ratings. It also holds continuous feedback, 360 rounds, check-ins, one-on-ones, initiatives and improvement plans.
M16.why: Without a prepared set-up and goal sheets, reviews have no fair basis and ratings cannot be compared. A cycle only moves when HR moves it, so an unattended cycle stalls and ratings never reach employees.
M16.who: Tenant Super Admin and Tenant HR Admin hold every performance right. Managers set goals, review and act for their team (performance.goals, review, feedback, team, initiatives); employees set own goals, review and give feedback. Auditors only view. The Performance Admin role template has no performance rights until you add them.
M16.where: People › Growth: Performance desk, Review cycles, Goals, Goal sheets, Goal requests, Appraisals, Review requests, Calibration, 9-box and the other registers. Settings: Admin › Setup › Performance. Policies: Workflows › Policies.
objectives: Prepare rating scales, competencies, KRAs, units, KPI formulas, review and goal templates for your organisation.
Launch a review cycle and move it through goal setting, reviews, calibration and the final rating to closure.
Calibrate, finalize and publish ratings, and follow feedback, 360 rounds, check-ins and improvement plans.

M06 Workflows and policies: goal sheet, performance, PIP and 360 feedback policies decide who gets which rules

M08 Letters: performance, PIP and PIP evaluation letter templates for the letters the policies draft

procedures.title: Prepare the performance set-up
procedures.before: Agree the rating scale, competencies and terminology with leadership.
steps: Open Admin › Setup and choose Performance. Set 'Cycle starting month', 'How do you want to publish performance rating?' and the terminology.
Open People › Growth › Rating scales. Edit the Five-point scale labels if needed, or add a scale and tick Default scale.
Open Competencies. Edit the six standard competencies or add your own with weights and behavioural indicators.
Add KRAs with suggested KPIs in KRA library, units in Units of measurement and formulas in KPI rating formulas.
Open Review templates, add a template, then Publish version: rating scale, competencies, stages and weights.
procedures.result: A published review template version and libraries ready for goal setting and reviews.

procedures.title: Prepare goal sheets for a cycle
procedures.before: A launched cycle with a Goal setting stage; goal templates if goals are standard.
steps: In Goal templates, click Add template. Enter KRAs and KPIs with weightage, or use Add from KRA library on the saved template.
In a goal sheet policy (Workflows › Policies) choose manual creation or system mapping, approval and weightage rules.
In Goals, click New goal, choose Company goal, add key results and an Owner.
Open Goal sheets, filter Sheet status = Not created or Draft (not submitted), and remind those employees.
Managers approve or send back sheets in My work › Inbox; follow them in Goal requests and use Extend goal if needed.
procedures.result: Every employee in the cycle has an active goal sheet whose weightage matches the required total.

procedures.title: Launch a review cycle
procedures.before: Rating scale, competencies, employees with current reporting managers and, if used, the performance policy.
steps: Open Review cycles and click New performance cycle. Enter Name, Code, Type, Period start and Period end.
Pick a Template version, or set Rating scale, Goals weight, Competencies weight and Competencies rated.
Check each stage's Starts on and Ends on. The suggested dates start after the period; move Goal setting if needed.
Choose Show self review to manager and peer anonymity. Add Eligibility conditions or leave empty for everyone.
On the Review step check the details and click Create performance cycle. The cycle opens on its edit page as Draft.
Click Launch cycle on the edit page or on the cycle's row in Review cycles. The dialog shows how many eligible employees get an appraisal. Confirm.
procedures.result: The cycle is Active at its first stage, each eligible employee has an appraisal with self and manager reviews, and the design is frozen.

procedures.title: Move a cycle through its stages
steps: On Review requests open the view Still to review; use Remind or bulk Remind reviewers.
Use Extend window (cycle) or Extend review for everyone or chosen employees, with a reason.
Use Add employees on the running cycle; they get an appraisal and the open stages' reviews.
When a stage is done, click Move to … on the cycle. Goals lock when the self review starts.
Moving to Calibration scores every open appraisal and sets them to Calibration.
procedures.result: The cycle reaches the Calibration or Final rating stage with reviews submitted.

procedures.title: Run calibration and publish ratings
procedures.before: The cycle is at its Calibration stage and manager reviews are submitted.
steps: Open People › Growth › Calibration and use Choose cycle. Use Filter for a department or grade.
Click Distribution targets and enter a % per level that adds up to 100 (optional).
Click Normalise ratings: choose Who, enter New normalised rating for each changed row, then one Reason.
Use Calibrate on a row: choose the Calibrated rating and write the note.
Use Finalize on each row: final rating (blank = calibrated or computed), summary, recommendations.
If publishing is manual, click Publish ratings. On the cycle use Move to … until it reads Close cycle, click it, and later Archive.
procedures.result: Ratings are final, published to employees, the cycle is closed and every appraisal is locked.

procedures.title: Run a 360 feedback round
procedures.before: Feedback templates for the '360 feedback' process and a published 360 feedback policy.
steps: Open 360 feedback rounds and click Launch 360 feedback. Choose the policy, a day in the period and the employees.
Open the round (View): Employees and nominations shows who still has to nominate and approvals waiting.
Use Extend window for everyone or chosen employees, with a reason.
Click Close round after the window, or let the daily job close it.
Use Export results for the CSV; employees and managers read results as the policy allows.
procedures.result: A closed round with aggregated results; if the policy blends it, linked appraisals are rescored.

procedures.title: Open and close an improvement plan
procedures.before: PIP reasons in Performance masters; a PIP policy if you need approval, letters or checklists.
steps: In Improvement plans click Open plan. Choose Employee and Manager, dates, PIP reasons, Reason and objectives.
If the plan shows Waiting for approval, HR uses Approve plan or Reject plan.
Use Add checkpoint and Review checkpoint during the plan; Extend if more time is needed.
Use Close with Successfully completed, Unsuccessful or Cancelled and the outcome text.
Approve outcome if asked, review close checkpoints, then Close plan with a reason.
procedures.result: A closed plan with its outcome, checkpoints and letters on record.

calculations.title: Goal progress from a check-in
calculations.intro: A check-in records a current value; progress is how far it has moved from the start value to the target, between 0 and 100 %. Example organisation: key result 'Cut p95 latency to 200ms'.
explain: Formula
(current − start) ÷ (target − start) × 100, kept between 0 and 100. Done / not done: 100 % when the value is 1 or more.
Where you see it
Progress column on Goals and on the goal's key results.

calculations.title: Roll-up to an aligned goal
calculations.intro: A goal without its own key results takes the weighted progress of the goals aligned to it. Example organisation: 'Ship platform v2 by Q3' has two aligned employee goals of weight 70 each.
total: Progress of 'Ship platform v2 by Q3'
explain: Formula
Σ(progress × weight) ÷ Σ weight; without weights, a plain average. The company goal above it also shows 57.50 %.
Where you see it
Progress column on Goals; Linked goals tab on the parent goal.

calculations.title: Computed rating of an appraisal
calculations.intro: Illustrative numbers on the 1–5 Five-point scale with the default weights (goals 70 %, competencies 30 %). The submitted manager review (or approver review) drives the score.
lines: Goal A rated 4: (4 − 1) ÷ 4 = 75 %, × weight 70 ÷ total weight 100
Goal B rated 3: (3 − 1) ÷ 4 = 50 %, × weight 30 ÷ total weight 100
Competency score: ratings 3 and 4 = 50 % and 75 %, plain average (no competency weights)
total: Computed rating (label: nearest level, Exceeds Expectations)
explain: Formula
Each rating is turned into a share of the scale, weighted, blended by the cycle weights and placed back on the scale.
What can change it
Goal sheet or performance policy weights, competency weights, periodic reviews, a blended 360 round, calibration.
Where you see it
Computed column on Appraisals and the Calibration board.

calculations.title: Suggested rating from a KPI rating formula
calculations.intro: Illustrative formula 'Achievement ÷ target' with bands 0–79.99 % → 2, 80–99.99 % → 3, 100–119.99 % → 4, 120 % and above → 5.
explain: Reverse KPI
Lower is better: target ÷ achievement instead, for example 200 ÷ 320 × 100 = 62.50 % → band 0–79.99 % → 2.
Key results
A goal with key results uses their weighted achievement.
Where you see it
On each goal of the review form when the formula rating is switched on.

troubleshooting: An appraisal has a self review but no manager review
The employee had no current reporting manager when the cycle launched (as for Anita Rao in the example).
Set the reporting manager, then use Add employees on the running cycle for that employee to add the open stages' reviews.
'Calibration has not opened yet.'
The cycle has not reached its Calibration stage.
Move the cycle to Calibration with Move to … first.
'The Manager review stage has not opened yet.' when submitting a review
Reviews can be submitted only once the cycle has reached their stage.
Move the cycle to that stage, then ask the reviewer again.
'Finalization opens at the calibration or final stage.'
Finalize was tried before the cycle reached Calibration or Final rating.
Move the cycle on, then finalize.
'The manager review is not submitted; provide a final rating explicitly.'
Finalize was left blank while the manager review is pending.
Remind the manager, or choose a Final rating in the Finalize dialog.
'N appraisal(s) are not finalized yet.' on Close cycle
Open appraisals remain.
Finalize them on the Calibration board, or withdraw people who left.
'Goal weights add up to X; this cycle requires Y.'
The goal sheet's weightage does not match the required total.
Change goal weights on Goals so they add up, then Submit goal sheet again.
'Goals of … can be changed only during the goal window'
Goal editing is limited to the goal-setting period or policy window.
Use Extend goal on Goal requests for the people who need time.
Reopen is not offered on Review requests
The setting 'HR may reopen a submitted review' is off, or the review is a peer review.
Switch it on in Admin › Setup › Performance; peers and 360 cannot be reopened.
Give feedback or My check-in is missing
Your sign-in is not linked to an employee record.
These are employee and manager actions; use an employee sign-in to try them.

M17.intro: This module covers what people learn and how they grow: the learning catalogue (courses, paths, programs, sessions), assignments, enrolments and certificates; skills, skill assessments and development plans; career tracks, paths and role requirements; and confidential talent and succession records.
M17.why: Mandatory training that is not assigned or tracked leaves compliance gaps and expired certificates. Without skills, role requirements and succession plans, critical roles have no prepared successors and development is not targeted.
M17.who: Tenant Super Admin and Tenant HR Admin hold the learning, skills, development and career rights and the talent and succession rights. Managers assign learning to their team, approve requests, assess skills and plan development; employees learn and keep their own skills and career profile. Auditors only view.
M17.where: People › Growth: Courses, Programs, Learning paths, Training sessions, Instructors, Providers, Assignments, Enrolments, Certificates, Learning overview, Skills, Skill levels, Skill assessments, Development plans, Career architecture, Career paths, Role requirements, Career profiles, Critical positions, Succession plans, Successors, Readiness, Development actions, Talent pools, Talent reviews, Talent overview, Talent analytics.
objectives: Build and publish courses, learning paths and programs, and assign mandatory learning to the right people.
Track enrolments, sessions, completions and certificates, and maintain skills, assessments and development plans.
Set up career paths and role requirements, designate critical positions, create succession plans and run talent reviews.
depends_on: M03 Organisation structure: designations (roles), job families, business units and organisation units
M07 Employees: current reporting managers decide whom managers may assign, assess and see
M16 Performance: competencies and development needs from appraisals and skill assessments
M04 Masters and configuration: Admin › Setup › Learning links, and Core HR 'Proficiency levels for profile skills and career path steps'
M06 Workflows and policies: rule conditions define populations for assignments

subs.name: Learning catalogue
subs.desc: Providers, instructors, courses with modules and assessments, learning paths and programs.

subs.name: Delivering learning
subs.desc: Training sessions, assignments (mandatory learning), enrolments, certificates and the learning overview.

subs.name: Skills and development plans
subs.desc: The skill library, skill levels, skill assessments and development plans.

subs.name: Career architecture
subs.desc: Career tracks, career paths with steps, role requirements and employees' career profiles.

subs.name: Succession
subs.desc: Critical positions, succession plans, successors, readiness and their development actions.

subs.name: Talent pools, reviews and analytics
subs.desc: Talent pools, talent review sessions and the talent overview and analytics.

people/providers.purpose: Organisations that deliver learning, internal L&D or external, with contact details. Courses and instructors can name a provider.
people/providers.when: Before you add courses delivered by an outside training company.
elements: Adds a provider: name, code, type, status, description and contact details.
Internal L&D or External provider; also a filter.
Number of instructors linked to the provider.

fields.label: Code
fields.meaning: Short unique code; fixed after saving.

fields.label: Status
fields.meaning: Active providers can be chosen on courses.

people/providers.after: The provider can be chosen on courses and instructors; completions record it.
people/providers.permission: learning.view to see; learning.manage to change.

people/instructors.purpose: People who teach courses: an employee (internal) or an external trainer, with provider, specialisation and bio.
people/instructors.when: Before you name an instructor on courses.
elements: Adds an internal instructor (pick the employee) or an external one (name and e-mail).
Internal with the employee code, or External.
Who they work for and what they teach.

fields.label: Internal instructor (employee)
fields.meaning: Pick an employee; leave blank for an external instructor.

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: Needed for an external instructor; taken from the employee record otherwise.

fields.label: Status
fields.meaning: Active instructors can be chosen on courses.

people/instructors.after: The instructor can be chosen on courses.
people/instructors.permission: learning.view to see; learning.manage to change.

people/courses.purpose: The learning catalogue: each course with type, category, duration, mandatory flag, certificate validity, modules, enrolments, version and status. The example has POSH awareness (active) and Fire safety drill (published).
people/courses.when: To add courses, send them for approval, publish new versions or retire them.
elements: Counts and quick views by status.
Sends the course to a second person with learning.publish.
Approver's decision, then publishing a new immutable version.
Stops new enrolments (with a reason); archive a retired course.
Lists the published versions with dates.
people/courses.permission: learning.view to see; learning.manage to create, submit, publish and retire; learning.publish to approve.
people/courses.depends: Providers and instructors if you name them.
people/courses.limits: A course must be approved by a second person with learning.publish before it is published; you cannot approve a course you submitted.

people/courses--create.purpose: Create a course in five steps: the course, its catalogue details, the rules (mandatory, approval, certificate, passing score), the skill outcomes and a review.
people/courses--create.when: When you add a new course to the catalogue.
elements: Title, code, type, category, duration, content link, owner, description.
Topic, difficulty, delivery mode, language, provider, instructor, cost, dates, prerequisites.
Mandatory, self-enrol, approval of requests, certificate validity, passing score, attempts.
Skill levels a completion records as verified.
Check the details, then create the course (it starts as Draft).

fields.label: Code
fields.meaning: Short unique code; used in certificate numbers.

fields.label: Type
fields.meaning: Video, Document / reading, E-learning (external link), Classroom, Virtual or Assessment only.

fields.label: Category
fields.meaning: Compliance, Onboarding, Technical, Leadership, Soft skills, Product, Health & safety, Other.

fields.label: Content url
fields.meaning: Link to the external LMS or video.

fields.label: Delivery mode
fields.meaning: Classroom, Virtual, Self-paced, Blended, On-the-job and others; self-paced modes let learners report progress.

fields.label: Employees may self-enrol
fields.meaning: Employees can request or join it themselves.

fields.label: Requests need approval
fields.meaning: Employee requests wait for a manager or L&D decision.

fields.label: Certificate valid for
fields.meaning: Months a certificate stays valid; blank = no expiry and no certificate.

fields.label: Passing score
fields.meaning: % needed to pass; blank = per assessment.

fields.label: Skill
fields.meaning: Skill outcome: the skill a completion evidences.

fields.label: Level
fields.meaning: A value on the skill's scale, recorded as verified on completion.

people/courses--create.after: The course is saved as Draft and opens for editing; add modules and an assessment, then Submit for approval.
people/courses--create.depends: Skills and providers if you use them.
people/courses--create.limits: Modules hold text or links; files cannot be uploaded as course content.

people/courses--edit.purpose: Change a course and build its content: modules in order and one assessment, with the course's history. The example opens POSH awareness with two text modules.
people/courses--edit.when: After creating a course, and before submitting a new version.
elements: Course, Catalogue, Rules, Skill outcomes, Review.
Tab: ordered content units (title, type, duration, link); Add module, Edit, Delete.
Tab: one quiz per course with passing score, time limit and questions; Add assessment.
Tab: every change to the course.
Why you changed it, kept in the audit trail.

fields.label: Correct option # (0-based)
fields.meaning: Assessment question: number of the right option, counting the first as 0.

people/courses--edit.after: Changes are saved. Learners keep the version they started; publish a new version for new learners.
people/courses--edit.limits: Assessments have single-choice questions only, one assessment per course; there is no question bank.

people/learning-paths.purpose: Ordered bundles of courses with required and optional items, in-path prerequisites and milestones, published as versions.
people/learning-paths.when: When a role needs a sequence of courses, for example onboarding.
elements: Number of courses in the path.
Snapshots items, prerequisites and milestones; learners keep the version they enrolled on.
people/learning-paths.permission: learning.view to see; learning.manage to change and publish.

people/learning-paths--create.purpose: Create a learning path: name, code, description, status and milestones. Courses are added on the saved path's Courses tab.
people/learning-paths--create.when: When you start a new path.
elements: Name, code, description, status and milestones.
Adds a milestone row: title and after which item it falls.
Check the details, then create the path.

fields.label: Code
fields.meaning: Short unique code; fixed after saving.

fields.label: Milestones
fields.meaning: Rows of Title and After item #.

people/learning-paths--create.after: The path is saved; on its edit page use Add course (course, order, required, prerequisites), then Publish version.
people/learning-paths--create.depends: Published or active courses to add.
people/learning-paths--create.limits: A path cannot be published without at least one course.

people/programs.purpose: Learning programs that combine courses and paths with a start and end, required and optional items, a completion rule and an optional program certificate.
people/programs.when: For cohort programmes such as a leadership programme.
elements: Starts on, Ends on, items (course or learning path, required), optional items to complete, certificate and validity.
Adds an employee to the current version.
Number of people on the current version.

fields.label: Code
fields.meaning: Short unique code; fixed after saving.

people/programs.after: Publish a version before enrolling. A participant completes when every required item and the chosen number of optional items are complete.
people/programs.permission: learning.view to see; learning.manage to change, publish and enrol.
people/programs.limits: A program certificate needs at least one course item.

people/training-sessions.purpose: Classroom and virtual deliveries of courses with trainer, venue or link, capacity and registrations. The example has 'Quarterly fire drill – Delhi', 30 seats, scheduled.
people/training-sessions.when: To schedule sessions and follow registrations and attendance.
elements: Registered people out of capacity, for example 0 / 30.
Employees register themselves (sign-ins linked to an employee).
Opens the session with its attendees.
Scheduled, Completed or Cancelled; also a filter.
people/training-sessions.permission: learning.view to see; learning.manage or learning.assign to schedule and mark attendance.
people/training-sessions.depends: A published course of type Classroom or Virtual.

people/training-sessions--create.purpose: Schedule a session of a classroom or virtual course: course, title, mode, status, trainer and seats, and when and where.
people/training-sessions--create.when: When a classroom or online session is planned.
elements: Internal trainer, external trainer and capacity.
Start, end, venue (classroom) or meeting link (virtual).

fields.label: Title
fields.meaning: Session name, for example Quarterly fire drill – Delhi.

fields.label: Capacity
fields.meaning: Seats; blank = unlimited. When full, new registrations are waitlisted.

fields.label: Ends at
fields.meaning: End date and time, after the start.

people/training-sessions--create.after: The session is listed as Scheduled; employees can register, and you can register people on its edit page.
people/training-sessions--create.depends: A published course of type Classroom or Virtual.

people/training-sessions--edit.purpose: Change a session, register employees, mark attendance and mark the session completed.
people/training-sessions--edit.when: Before the session to register people, and after it to record attendance.
elements: Session, Trainer and seats, When and where, Review.
Code, Employee, Status, Enrolment and Rating of each attendee.
Registers an employee; an enrolment is created for them.
Records attendance; Attended completes the enrolment unless an assessment remains.

fields.label: Course
fields.meaning: The course delivered (example: Fire safety drill).

people/training-sessions--edit.after: Attendance completes enrolments; certificates follow when the course has a validity period.
people/training-sessions--edit.limits: Mark session completed only changes the session's status; mark each attendee Attended or Absent yourself.

people/assignments.purpose: Who must learn what: a course or path assigned to one employee, a manager's team, an organisation unit or a rule-defined population, with due days, repeat and mandatory flag. Example: 'PoSH for everyone (annual)'.
people/assignments.when: To assign mandatory or recommended learning, and to re-apply it to new joiners.
elements: Creates the assignment and enrols the matching people at once.
Days to complete (30 d) and the repeat interval (12 mo) in the example.
Number of enrolments the assignment created (5 in the example).
Enrols people who match now and are not yet covered.
Changes make a new version; Cancel (with a reason) cancels enrolments not yet started.

fields.label: Course
fields.meaning: Published or active course; required unless a path is chosen.

fields.label: or learning path
fields.meaning: An active learning path instead of a course.

fields.label: Target
fields.meaning: One employee, A manager's team, An organisation unit or A rule-defined population.

fields.label: Manager (their team) / Organisation unit
fields.meaning: For a team or an organisation unit.

fields.label: Keep enrolling people who match later (daily)
fields.meaning: Enrols new matches, for example joiners, every day.

fields.label: Conditions
fields.meaning: Rules that narrow the target; empty population = everyone employed.

fields.label: Due within
fields.meaning: Days from enrolment to the due date.

fields.label: Repeat every
fields.meaning: Months until people are enrolled again; blank = once.

people/assignments.after: Matching employees are enrolled as Assigned with a due date; a daily job enrols new matches and re-enrols when the repeat or a certificate expires.
people/assignments.permission: learning.manage for any target; learning.assign for employees and teams one manages.
people/assignments.depends: A published or active course, or an active learning path.
people/assignments.limits: An organisation unit target enrols only people placed directly in that unit, not in its sub-units; use conditions or one assignment per unit.

people/enrolments.purpose: Every learner on every course with status, progress, due date, mandatory flag, score and completion. Example: 5 POSH awareness enrolments, Assigned, due 16 Dec 2026.
people/enrolments.when: To follow progress and overdue learning, and to assign learning to one person.
elements: Employee, course or learning path, due date and reason.
Assigned, Requested, Pending approval, Enrolled, Waitlisted, Started, Overdue, Completed, Failed and others.
Shown in red when an open enrolment is past due.
people/enrolments.permission: learning.view to see all; learning.team for one's team; learning.assign or learning.manage to assign.

people/enrolments--view.purpose: One learner's enrolment: status, progress, due date, score, attempts, completion and expiry, the course content link and the modules done.
people/enrolments--view.when: To help a learner, record a completion or correct one.
elements: Sets progress %; progress is not completion.
Adds a PDF or image as evidence.
Record completion, Correct completion, Approve, Reject, Cancel, Withdraw when they apply.
people/enrolments--view.permission: learning.view; learning.manage to record or correct a completion.
people/enrolments--view.limits: A completion is final: correcting it creates a new, audited record and the original stays as superseded.

people/certificates.purpose: Certificates issued on completion of courses with a validity period, and external certificates you record, with number, dates, verification and status.
people/certificates.when: To check who holds valid certificates, record external ones and revoke wrong ones.
elements: Employee, learning item, credential number, issuer, dates, link and file.
Valid, Expiring, Expired or Revoked; also a filter.
Verified or Unverified; external certificates start unverified.
Open the certificate document, or attach a PDF.
Verify an external certificate; revoke with a reason (final).
people/certificates.after: The certificate is listed. A daily job moves certificates to Expiring and Expired; recurring assignments then enrol the person again.
people/certificates.permission: learning.view to see; learning.certificates to record, verify and revoke.
people/certificates.limits: Certificate documents PeopleOS generates are web (HTML) pages, not PDFs. A holder can never verify their own certificate.

people/learning-overview.purpose: Organisation-wide learning figures: enrolments, completion rate, mandatory compliance, learning hours, certificates, development plans, popular courses, skill gaps, departments, providers and costs.
people/learning-overview.when: Monthly, or before an audit of mandatory training.
elements: Enrolments / Completion rate / Mandatory compliance / Learning hours
Headline figures; enrolments count the last 12 months, hours come from final completions.
Per course: Assigned, Completed, Overdue and Compliance.
Aggregates; groups smaller than 5 people are suppressed.
people/learning-overview.permission: learning.analytics, learning.view or learning.manage; costs need learning.costs.
people/learning-overview.limits: Groups of fewer than 5 people are hidden to protect individuals.

people/skills.purpose: The skill library (9 skills in the example, such as PHP, Laravel and Leadership) with category, type, proficiency scale and validity.
people/skills.when: Before skills are assessed, required by roles or recorded as course outcomes.
elements: Name, code, category, type, description, proficiency scale, status and dates.
Free grouping, for example technical or behavioural.
Filter on active or inactive skills.

fields.label: Type
fields.meaning: Technical, Behavioural, Functional, Leadership, Domain, Digital or Language.

fields.label: Proficiency scale
fields.meaning: Scale for levels; blank = the default scale.

people/skills.after: The skill can be assessed, required by roles and career steps, and recorded by courses.
people/skills.permission: skills.view to see; skills.manage to change.

people/skill-levels.purpose: Proficiency scales for skills, published as versions. The example has Proficiency v1: 1 Beginner, 2 Intermediate, 3 Advanced, 4 Expert.
people/skill-levels.when: Before assessing skills, or when you need a different scale.
elements: Value, label, description and behavioural indicator per level; at least two levels.
Earlier versions; assessments keep the version they used.
people/skill-levels.after: A new version of levels applies to new assessments and requirements; older ones keep theirs.
people/skill-levels.permission: skills.view to see; skills.manage to change.
people/skill-levels.limits: Levels on different scales are never converted; role gaps compare levels on the same scale only.

people/skill-assessments.purpose: Assessed skill levels per employee: self, manager, formal or certification assessments, with evidence, target level and private notes.
people/skill-assessments.when: When managers or L&D assess skills, for example after training or in a review.
elements: Employee, skill, type, level, target level, valid until, evidence, comments, private notes.
Comments, evidence, private notes (if you may read them) and corrections.
Locks the assessment; optionally records a development need for the gap to the target.
Creates a corrected assessment with a reason; the original is superseded.

fields.label: Type
fields.meaning: Self, Manager, Formal assessment or Certification.

fields.label: Level
fields.meaning: A value on the skill's scale.

fields.label: Valid until
fields.meaning: When the assessment should be repeated.

fields.label: Evidence
fields.meaning: What the level is based on.

people/skill-assessments.after: The assessment is a draft until finalized; a finalized level updates the employee's skill profile.
people/skill-assessments.permission: skills.assess (people one manages), skills.manage (formal and certification), skills.private_notes to read notes.
people/skill-assessments.depends: Skills and a published skill scale.

people/development-plans.purpose: Development plans per employee with items (goals, skill gaps, learning, milestones, reviews), target date, progress and status.
people/development-plans.when: After reviews or skill assessments, to plan how a person develops.
elements: Employee, title, summary, dates and private notes; the employee's open development needs are added.
The plan's items with learning suggestions for skill gaps.
Add item / Enrol learning / Complete item
Add items, enrol the person in an item's course, close an item.
Draft → Active ⇄ On hold → Completed or Cancelled → Archived.
people/development-plans.after: The plan is created with the employee's open development needs as items. Courses are suggested, never enrolled automatically.
people/development-plans.permission: development.view to see all; development.own, development.team or development.manage to change.
people/development-plans.limits: Completed and cancelled plans are read-only.

people/career-architecture.purpose: Career tracks: the kinds of careers your organisation offers (individual contributor, people manager, specialist, leadership).
elements: Code, name, track type, status and description.
Individual contributor, People manager, Technical specialist, Functional specialist or Leadership.
Change a track or retire it.

fields.label: Code
fields.meaning: Short unique code; fixed after saving.

people/career-architecture.after: The track can be chosen on career paths and career profiles.
people/career-architecture.permission: career.view to see; career.manage to change.

people/career-paths.purpose: Career ladders of designations with typical years and required skills, published as versions. The example has Engineering ladder: Software Engineer → Engineering Manager → Chief Technology Officer, not yet published.
people/career-paths.when: To show employees how they can progress and what skills the next step needs.
elements: Snapshots the steps with an effective date.
Change the path and its steps.
people/career-paths.permission: career.view to see; career.manage to change and publish.
people/career-paths.depends: Designations, job families and career tracks.

people/career-paths--create.purpose: Create a career path: name, code, status, where it applies (job family, track, business unit, organisation unit) and effective dates.
people/career-paths--create.when: When you define a new ladder.
elements: Job family, career track, business unit, organisation unit.

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: Path name, for example Engineering ladder.

fields.label: Code
fields.meaning: Short unique code; fixed after saving.

fields.label: Job family
fields.meaning: Job family it belongs to; blank = any.

people/career-paths--create.after: The path is saved; add steps on its Steps tab, then Publish version.

people/career-paths--edit.purpose: Change a career path and its steps: each step's designation, order, typical years and required skills.
people/career-paths--edit.when: When you build or change the ladder before publishing.
elements: Career path, Where it applies, Effective dates, Review.
Tab: the ladder; Add step with designation, sort order, typical years and required skills.

fields.label: Designation
fields.meaning: Step: the role at this step.

fields.label: Typical years at this step
fields.meaning: Step: usual time in the role.

people/career-paths--edit.after: Changes are saved; use Publish version on Career paths so passports and gaps use them.
people/career-paths--edit.limits: A path cannot be published without at least one step.

people/role-requirements.purpose: What a role (designation, optionally in one unit) requires: skills with levels, a primary skill, competencies, experience, certifications and learning, as dated versions.
people/role-requirements.when: To measure people against a role, for example successors against a critical position.
elements: Role, unit, effective date, skills, competencies, experience, certifications, learning, notes.
Each publish is a new version; the previous one closes.
The main skill and minimum years.

fields.label: Skill / level
fields.meaning: Each skill with a level on its current scale; Required and Primary skill toggles.

people/role-requirements.after: A new version applies from its date; gaps for career profiles and successors are worked out against it.
people/role-requirements.permission: career.view to see; career.manage to publish.
people/role-requirements.depends: Designations, skills with published levels, competencies and courses.
people/role-requirements.limits: Only one primary skill per version, and each skill once.

people/career-profiles.purpose: Employees' career profiles: track, target roles and whether they share aspirations and mobility with their manager. Employees maintain them in My career.
people/career-profiles.when: To see career interests across the organisation, for example before talent reviews.
elements: What the employee shares with their manager (off by default).
History of short, medium and long term aspirations.
people/career-profiles.limits: HR cannot create a profile here; only the employee changes sharing choices.

people/critical-positions.purpose: Roles (designation, optionally in one unit) designated as critical, with a criticality assessment, review frequency, open plan and next review date.
people/critical-positions.when: When you start succession planning and at each position review.
elements: Role, unit, title, review frequency and the criticality assessment.
Current incumbents, a recorded incumbent exit and earlier assessments.
Records a new criticality assessment with a reason.
Vacancy risk, review date and confidential notes.
Ends the designation with a reason.
In red when overdue; Status filter defaults to Active.

fields.label: Title
fields.meaning: Name of the position, for example Head of Finance.

fields.label: Business impact / Talent scarcity / Replacement difficulty / Operational dependency

people/critical-positions.after: The position is active; create its succession plan from the row.
people/critical-positions.permission: succession.view to see; succession.manage to designate, assess and plan.
people/critical-positions.limits: A position is a role, not a single seat; a unit matches only that unit, not its sub-units.

people/succession-plans.purpose: One succession plan per critical position with its successors, vacancy risk, review date and status (draft, active, under review, closed).
people/succession-plans.when: To add successors and keep plans current.
elements: The plan's successors with their readiness; confidential notes for talent.confidential.
Employee, strengths, development gaps, confidential notes.
Draft → Active ⇄ Under review → Closed (reason needed when closing).
people/succession-plans.permission: succession.view to see; succession.manage to change.
people/succession-plans.depends: A critical position: plans are created there with Create succession plan.
people/succession-plans.limits: Only one open plan per position; closed plans are read-only.

people/successors.purpose: Everyone named as a successor, with the critical position, current readiness and status.
people/successors.when: To record readiness and plan development for successors.
elements: Readiness, reason, evidence and effective date.
Adds a learning, skill, project, mentoring or other action to the successor's development plan.
Removes the successor with a reason (kept in history).
people/successors.permission: succession.view; succession.assess to record readiness; succession.manage for actions and removal.
people/successors.limits: The development action title is shown to the employee in their plan: keep it neutral and never mention succession.

people/readiness.purpose: Readiness assessments: how ready a person is for a critical position or a role (Ready now, Ready < 1 year, Ready 1–2 years, Longer term, Not assessed).
people/readiness.when: At talent reviews and plan reviews.
elements: Employee, critical position or role, readiness, reason, evidence, effective date.
Readiness stays valid 12 months; shown in red when past.
Current or Superseded; filter defaults to Current.

fields.label: …or a role
fields.meaning: A designation instead of a position.

people/readiness.after: The new assessment becomes current and supersedes the previous one for the same target.
people/readiness.permission: succession.view to see; succession.assess to record.
people/readiness.limits: Readiness is a recorded judgement; PeopleOS never calculates it.

people/development-actions.purpose: Development actions agreed for successors, each linked to an item of the employee's development plan, with type, due date and progress.
people/development-actions.when: To follow whether successors' development happens.
elements: Learning path, certification, skill, project, mentoring, coaching, stretch, rotation and others.
The item in the development plan the employee sees.
The critical position the action supports.
Due date and the plan item's status.
people/development-actions.depends: Actions are created from Successors › Development action.
people/development-actions.limits: Read-only list; progress is updated on the development plan item.

people/talent-pools.purpose: Named groups of people for development or succession (for example future leaders), with explicit, dated membership and reasons.
people/talent-pools.when: After talent reviews, to keep the pools current.
elements: Code, name, description, criteria for nominators, status.
Active members you may see, with the date and reason.
Member and a reason; history is kept.

fields.label: Code
fields.meaning: Short unique code; fixed after saving.

fields.label: Criteria (for the people who nominate — nothing is applied automatically)

people/talent-pools.after: The pool is listed; add members with Add members.
people/talent-pools.permission: talent.view to see; talent.manage to change.
people/talent-pools.limits: Membership is never automatic: criteria are guidance for the people who nominate.

people/talent-reviews.purpose: Talent review sessions: a named meeting with a scope, participants, a population of employees and a recorded decision per person.
people/talent-reviews.when: Once or twice a year, often after the performance cycle.
elements: Name, scope (organisation unit), participants, scheduled date.
See and add the employees to discuss.
Moves the session to in progress.
Completes with a summary, or cancels with a reason.

fields.label: Participants
fields.meaning: Users who take part; they see only their sessions.

people/talent-reviews.after: The session is a draft until started; decisions become read-only once recorded or the session ends.
people/talent-reviews.permission: talent.manage to create and manage; talent.review to take part and record decisions.
people/talent-reviews.limits: Decisions are records only: adding to a pool, naming a successor or a development action is a separate step by a person.

people/talent-overview.purpose: Talent and succession at a glance: critical positions, coverage with successors, ready-now successors, open plans, positions without a ready-now successor and talent pools.
people/talent-overview.when: Before leadership meetings and talent reviews.
elements: With successors / With a ready-now successor
Positions covered and the share of positions.
Plans that are draft, active or under review.
Pools with members; small pools are suppressed.
people/talent-overview.limits: Groups smaller than 5 people are suppressed.

people/talent-analytics.purpose: Aggregated succession and talent analytics: bench strength by critical position, readiness, development actions, review decisions, aspirations, mobility and successors' skill and certification gaps.
elements: Criticality, open plan, successors, ready now, next review, recorded incumbent exit.
Required skills and missing or expired certifications.
people/talent-analytics.depends: Critical positions, successors, readiness, role requirements.
people/talent-analytics.limits: People counts below 5 are suppressed; no score or ranking of people is shown.

procedures.title: Build and publish a course
procedures.before: Providers and instructors if needed; a colleague with 'Approve catalogue items for publication' (learning.publish).
steps: Open Courses and click New course. Fill Title, Code, Type, Category, then the Catalogue, Rules and Skill outcomes steps.
Tick Mandatory (compliance) for compliance training and enter Certificate valid for (months) if a certificate is needed.
On the edit page, Modules tab: Add module for each part. Assessment tab: Add assessment with questions.
On Courses use Submit for approval on the course's row.
Your colleague uses Approve (or Send back) on the row.
Use Publish version. The course becomes Published and can be assigned.
procedures.result: A published, versioned course ready for assignments, sessions and paths.

procedures.title: Assign mandatory learning
procedures.before: A published or active course (for example POSH awareness) or an active learning path.
steps: Open Assignments and click Assign learning. Enter a Name and choose the Course.
Target: A rule-defined population (empty conditions = everyone), an organisation unit, a team or one employee.
Leave Keep enrolling people who match later (daily) on so joiners are enrolled.
Due within 30 days, Repeat every 12 months for annual training, tick Mandatory and Required.
Create the assignment. Matching employees are enrolled at once as Assigned.
Check Enrolments (filter Status) and Learning overview › Mandatory training.
procedures.result: Every matching employee has an enrolment with a due date; new joiners and repeats are enrolled daily.

procedures.title: Run a classroom session
procedures.before: A published course of type Classroom training or Virtual training.
steps: Open Training sessions, click Schedule session, choose Course, Title, Mode, then trainer, Capacity, Starts at and Ends at.
Open the session (Edit) and use Register employee in Attendees, or let employees use Register me.
Mark each attendee Attended or Absent, or select rows and use Mark attended.
procedures.result: Attended enrolments are completed (unless an assessment remains) and certificates are issued when the course has a validity.

procedures.title: Assess a skill and plan development
procedures.before: Skills with a published skill scale.
steps: Open Skill assessments and click New assessment: Employee, Skill, Type, Level and Target level.
Use Finalize; tick Record a development need for the gap to the target if there is a gap.
Open Development plans and click New plan for the employee; open needs are added as items.
Use Add item with a Course, then Enrol learning on that item.
Use Change status to Active; complete items as they are done.
procedures.result: A finalized skill level, a development need and an active plan with learning.

procedures.title: Publish a career path and role requirements
steps: Open Career paths and click New career path: Name, Code, Status, where it applies and dates.
On the Steps tab use Add step: Designation, Sort order, Typical years at this step and Required skills.
On Career paths use Publish version with the effective date.
Open Role requirements, click Publish requirements: Role, skills with levels, competencies, experience and learning.
procedures.result: A published ladder and dated role requirements used for career passports and gaps.

procedures.title: Create a succession plan
procedures.before: The role exists as a designation; role requirements help to judge successors.
steps: Open Critical positions, click Designate critical position: Role, Title, Review every (months), criticality ratings and Reason.
On the position's row use Create succession plan: vacancy risk, review date, confidential notes.
Open Succession plans, use Add successor for each candidate with strengths and development gaps.
On Successors use Record readiness: Readiness, Reason, Evidence.
Use Development action with a neutral title, course or skill and due date.
On Succession plans use Change status → Active.
procedures.result: An active plan with successors, current readiness and development actions in their plans.

procedures.title: Run a talent review
procedures.before: Participants with talent.review; performance ratings and readiness up to date.
steps: Open Talent reviews, click New talent review: Name, Scope, Participants, Scheduled for.
Use Add employees to build the population.
Use Record decision for each employee: decision and reason.
Use Complete with a summary. Then add pool members or successors as agreed.
procedures.result: A completed review with a recorded decision per person; follow-ups done in Talent pools and Succession plans.

calculations.title: Due date of assigned learning
calculations.intro: Example organisation: the assignment 'PoSH for everyone (annual)' enrolled 5 employees on 16 Nov 2026 with Due within 30 days and Repeat every 12 months.
explain: Formula
Due on = the day the person is enrolled + Due within days; a joiner enrolled later gets a later due date.
Certificate
Completion date + Certificate valid for (12 months for POSH) gives Expires on.
Where you see it
Due on on Enrolments; Expires on on Certificates.

calculations.title: Mandatory training compliance
calculations.intro: Illustrative: 5 people assigned mandatory POSH awareness, 4 completed. In the example organisation today 0 of 5 are completed, so compliance is 0.0 %.
lines: Mandatory enrolments (not cancelled, rejected or withdrawn)
explain: Formula
Completed mandatory enrolments ÷ all mandatory enrolments × 100, one decimal.
Where you see it
Learning overview: Mandatory compliance and the Mandatory training table.

warnings.title: Publishing a course needs a second person
warnings.headline: You cannot publish a course you submitted yourself.
warnings.body: A course must be approved by a second person with 'Approve catalogue items for publication' (learning.publish) before Publish version is offered. The submitter never approves.
points: Give a colleague learning.publish.
Plan time for approval before an assignment deadline.
warnings.todo: Submit for approval, ask the colleague to Approve, then Publish version.

warnings.title: Certificates only for courses with a validity
warnings.headline: A completed course issues a certificate only when 'Certificate valid for' is set.
warnings.body: Courses without a validity record a completion but no certificate. Generated certificate documents are web pages; print them to PDF if a PDF is needed.
points: Set Certificate valid for on compliance courses.
Record external certificates with Record external certificate.
warnings.todo: Check the Rules step of each certified course.

warnings.title: Organisation unit targets do not include sub-units
warnings.headline: An assignment to an organisation unit enrols only people placed directly in that unit.
warnings.body: Employees in its sub-units are not included. A rule-defined population or one assignment per unit covers them.
points: Use A rule-defined population for 'everyone in a division'.
warnings.todo: Check the Enrolments count after Assign learning.

warnings.title: Course content and assessments are simple
warnings.headline: Modules hold text or links; assessments are single-choice quizzes, one per course.
warnings.body: Files cannot be uploaded as course content and SCORM packages are not supported. The correct option of a question is numbered from 0.
points: Host videos and documents elsewhere and link them.
Option 1 in the list is answer 0.
warnings.todo: Test the assessment with a colleague before publishing.

warnings.title: Succession is confidential
warnings.headline: Talent and succession records are not shown to the employee concerned.
warnings.body: An employee sees their own candidacy only with succession.own_candidacy, which no standard role gives. Notifications never tell them. Development action titles do appear in their development plan.
points: Keep development action titles neutral.
Give talent.confidential only to people who must read confidential notes; each read is audited.
warnings.todo: Review who holds talent and succession rights.

warnings.title: Talent decisions do not act on their own
warnings.headline: Review decisions, pool criteria and readiness are records; nothing is applied automatically.
warnings.body: Adding someone to a pool, naming a successor or starting development is always a separate action by a person.
points: After a review, add members and successors yourself.
warnings.todo: Use the decisions list as your follow-up checklist.

troubleshooting: 'This course must be approved by a second person (learning.publish) before it is published.'
Catalogue approval is required and the course is not approved.
Use Submit for approval and ask a colleague with learning.publish to Approve.
A course is missing from the session's Course list
Sessions offer only published courses of type Classroom training or Virtual training.
Set the course type and publish a version.
A course is missing from Assign learning
Only Published or Active courses can be assigned.
Publish the course first.
No certificate after completion
The course has no 'Certificate valid for'.
Set it and publish a new version; record past ones as external certificates.
A joiner was not enrolled
'Keep enrolling people who match later (daily)' is off, or the person is outside the target.
Use Apply now on the assignment, or edit it.
'A learning path needs at least one item.'
Publish version was used before courses were added.
Add courses on the path's Courses tab, then publish.
'Level X is not on the scale of …'
The level is not a value of the skill's current scale (Proficiency: 1–4).
Enter a level from the skill's scale.
New registrations show as waitlisted
The session is full (Registered = Capacity).
Raise Capacity or schedule another session.

Mandatory flag, Certificate valid for, modules and assessment; approved and published.
Population, due days, repeat 12 months, daily enrolment on.
Enrolments filtered by Overdue; reminders run daily.
Expiring and expired certificates reviewed; external ones verified.
Skill library and proficiency levels published; assessments finalized.
Plans active for open needs from reviews and assessments.
No overdue Next review; every position has a plan.
Readiness recorded within 12 months; development actions due.
Decisions recorded and followed up in pools and plans.
summary: Courses need approval by a second person before they can be published and assigned.
Assign learning enrols the target at once; a daily job adds joiners and repeats.
Certificates are issued only for courses with a validity period.
Skills, assessments and development plans turn needs into planned learning.
Critical positions, succession plans, successors and readiness are confidential records.
Talent decisions are recorded only; follow-up actions are always taken by people.

gaps: The example organisation has no providers, instructors, learning paths, programs, certificates, skill assessments, development plans, career tracks or profiles, role requirements, critical positions, succession plans, talent pools or reviews: those screens were captured empty.

Modal forms (Publish version for paths, programs and career paths, Assign learning, Record external certificate, New assessment, New plan, Designate critical position, Add successor, New talent review) are described from source, not from the crawl.
The items under 'More' on the enrolment view and the Attendees list on the session edit page were taken from source and the screenshot; the crawl did not list them.
Self-service screens employees use (My learning, My career, Register me) are not visible to the administrator sign-in, which is not linked to an employee.
Whether a succession plan or talent review is approved by a workflow depends on a set-up made by PeopleOS; without it, activating a plan and completing a review take effect at once.
